7

8

Magar baba se kehna, ab aana Shaam aana
Ya Husain, ya Husain
Magar baba se kehna, ab aana Shaam aana

9
Karo Rehaan o Sarwar aah o zaari
Sakina ne woh shab kaise guzaari
Tha sar godi mein shah ka, laboṅ par tha ye nauha
Ya Husain, ya Husain
Tha sar godi mein shah ka, laboṅ par tha ye nauha\"\"\"
roman_blocks = [b.splitlines() for b in roman.split('\\n\\n')]
source_blocks = [b.splitlines() for b in body.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
assert [len(b) for b in roman_blocks] == [len(b) for b in source_blocks]
for i, (r, u) in enumerate(zip(roman_blocks[1:], source_blocks[1:]), 1):
    assert r[0] == str(i) and u[0] == '۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹'[i-1]
    assert [j for j, line in enumerate(r) if line == 'Ya Husain, ya Husain'] == [j for j, line in enumerate(u) if line == 'یا حسینؑ، یا حسینؑ']
assert re.fullmatch(r'[\\x20-\\x7e\\nṅṄ]+', roman)
new = head.split('\\nromanLyrics:', 1)[0] + '\\nromanLyrics: |-\\n' + '\\n'.join('  ' + line if line else '' for line in roman.splitlines()) + '\\n---\\n' + body
p.write_text(new)
assert p.read_text().split('\\n---\\n', 1)[1] == body
print(sum(map(len, roman_blocks)) - 9, 'aligned verse lines')

item.text:
Audited the Roman transliteration against all 48 Urdu verse lines. Restored the missing fifth stanza and Refrain lines, corrected phonetic spellings, and aligned the opening and all nine stanzas. The Urdu body is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Human editorial sign-off remains pending. In stanza 2, I retained the existing Roman reading `hata do` because the Urdu reads `یٹا دو`. That discrepancy needs verification.
